Hi Jonas —

Thanks for sending the updated MSA and order form. Our legal team flagged a couple of publicity and confidentiality items that we need clarified before procurement can sign:

- We need explicit carveouts permitting us to reference the engagement in customer lists, but only in the context of sales collateral.
- Logo use needs to be limited to the product badge; we cannot have vendor corporate marks appearing on our public site without a separate approval cycle.
- We would like a 30-day quiet period post-launch before any press release.

I've attached a short PDF with the specific ACME requests. Can Redwood confirm whether the publicity clause (section 7) can be narrowed and whether you can accept a written approval workflow for logos/quotes?

Attachments: Acme_Publicity_Requests.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick response from Redwood side and a proposed path forward:

1) Customer lists / references: we can allow "Customer name and logo" in non-confidential sales collateral provided there is an approval step. We propose a clause that requires written approval (email OK) and a sample one-sentence attribution.

2) Logo usage: agree to limit to the product badge. We'll add language that prohibits modifications and use for co-branding without a separate trademark license.

3) Quiet period: we usually accept up to 30 days; we can agree to 30 days post-launch for Redwood marketing activity.

I've attached a redline with the proposed edits to section 7 and a short paragraph to add to the order form. Key points in the redline:
- \"Publicity and Reference\": Redwood may use Customer name/logo for sales reference purposes only after Customer's prior written approval (approval to be provided within 10 business days).
- \"Logo usage specification\": only product badge; no corporate marks; no modifications.
- \"Quotes\": short quote (<= 50 words) and final approval by Customer.

Attachments: ACME_MSAR_Redline_jonas.docx (docx)

Marissa — FYI on timing. Kimberly — looping you in for legal input on the approval SLA and whether 10 business days is acceptable.

Best,

On Wed, Jul 14, 2026 at 10:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a redline with the proposed edits to section 7...

Hi all —

Thanks, Jonas. From a legal perspective we want to:

- Keep approvals in writing (email is fine) but extend the review SLA to 15 business days for any quoted language to ensure Legal/PR review on both sides.
- Limit quotes to an "approved short excerpt" (<= 40 words) and require a final sign-off from Acme marketing.
- For logo use, require use only of the product badge provided by Acme; Redwood will not use Acme corporate marks or place the logo in a manner that implies endorsement of Acme's products.
- Include a simple termination carveout: if either party terminates for convenience prior to public reference, any in-flight approvals are revoked.

Suggested contract language snippet (for insertion into publicity clause):
"Either party may include the other party's name and product logo in customer lists and sales collateral, subject to prior written approval (which shall not be unreasonably withheld) and the following: (i) any quote shall be a short excerpt (no more than forty (40) words) and is subject to written approval by the referenced party's marketing representative; (ii) logo usage shall be limited to the product badge provided by the referenced party and shall not be altered; (iii) public announcements referencing the engagement shall not occur sooner than thirty (30) days after the go-live date; (iv) approvals related to quotes or logo usage shall be provided within fifteen (15) business days of a request, unless otherwise agreed in writing."

I'm attaching our internal publicity guidance for reference; it includes a recommended approval flow (owner, marketing, legal) and a template approval email. If Acme's counsel needs to preserve different SLAs, happy to negotiate.

Attachments: publicity_guidance_redwood.pdf (pdf)

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Acme's position is:

- We can accept an approval SLA of 15 business days for quoted language, but we request 10 business days for simple logo approvals (product badge usage) to avoid blocking marketing timelines.
- Regarding the 30 day quiet period: Acme's product team would like a 45-day quiet period for press announcements tied to broader go-to-market plans. Can we agree to 30 days for Redwood-initiated marketing and 45 days for joint press?
- We will provide a counter-redline that keeps the approval workflow but carves out one-off customer testimonial quotes that may be approved faster by Acme marketing.

Please see attached counter redline for section 7. We propose specific language for a two-track approval: logo (10 business days) and quote (15 business days), and a joint press escalation path.

Attachments: ACME_Counter_Redlines.docx (docx)

If Redwood can confirm willingness to accept the two-track SLA and the separate quiet periods, Acme can commit to finalizing order form signature by July 25.
